note: FNS 1070 establishes a general principle that income from ineligible household members is handled differently depending on the reason for ineligibility, with two categories: (1) income counted entirely (IPV, felony drug conviction, fleeing felon, workfare/work requirement sanctions per 1070.1) and (2) income prorated (SSN disqualification, comparable disqualification, child support disqualification, ineligible ABAWDs, ineligible non-citizens per 1070.2). The OLG covers some categories well but lacks others and has no unified framework. For prorated income: ABAWD disqualification is covered in excellent detail on the ABAWD Work Rules Disqualification Process page with step-by-step proration formulas; ineligible noncitizen income is covered thoroughly on the Calculation Rules and Attribution of Income for Mixed Noncitizen Households page with the combination calculation method. For income counted entirely: the Nonhousehold Members page states 'Except for people who have been disqualified, the nonhousehold member's income and resources are not to be considered,' implying disqualified members' income IS considered, but the OLG never explicitly states that income from IPV-disqualified, fleeing felon, drug felony, or voluntary quit members is counted in its entirety. The IPV Overview references the SNAP Attributed Amount (Riverside Rule), which is about preventing benefit increases from other-program sanctions — not about counting the disqualified member's own income. Missing from the OLG: (1) a unified explanation of the general principle that income treatment varies by ineligibility reason, (2) explicit rule that IPV/fleeing felon/drug felony/work sanction disqualified members' income is counted entirely, (3) income proration rules for SSN disqualification and child support disqualification categories.
